A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] served as '''Queen of Naboo''' during the height of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. She wore the traditional [[Clothing/Legends|garb]] and makeup of her predecessors on the throne of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and was known to enjoy open-air activities like [[Guarlara/Legends|guarlara]]-riding or [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]] with her pet [[twirrl]]s.

==Biography==
At some point following the [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|establishment]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="WoSW" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> a young [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] became the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] of the Human [[Naboo (people)/Legends|people]] living on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]],<ref name="WoSW" /> the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]].<ref name="EAWGG">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> When the famous [[Zoologist/Legends|zoologist]] [[Lyrre T'enna]] came to observe the Nabooian wildlife, the [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] allowed her access to the royal [[twirrling]], [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]], and [[Guarlara/Legends|guarlara]]-riding parties. T'enna made on-the-fly drawings of the Queen with her mounts, pet [[twirrl]]s, [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]], and [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Nabooian Royal Guards]]. The monarch was also depicted holding [[Voorpak/Legends|voorpaks]], diminutive furballs traditionally kept as mascots by [[Noble/Legends|noblewomen]]. T'enna's [[Color/Legends|colored]] renderings eventually appeared in the [[Lyrre T'enna's annotated field guide|published version]] of her field journal.<ref name="WoSW" />

==Personality and traits==
At the time of Lyrre T'enna's visit, the Queen of Naboo was a youthful-looking woman with reddish brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]], pale skin, and gray [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="WoSW" />

==Equipment==
The Queen wore the heavy, intricate, and highly-codified [[Clothing/Legends|regalia]] of the [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House]], some of which were dyed in an array of pastel colors.<ref name="WoSW" /> Like [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], one of her predecessors during the last [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TPMV">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> the Queen sported traditional make-up, including stylized beauty marks and the red [[Scar of remembrance/Legends|scar of remembrance]]<ref name="WoSW" />&mdash;a symbol of remembrance for Naboo's [[Time of Suffering/Legends|Time of Suffering]] before the [[Great Time of Peace/Legends|Great Time of Peace]],<ref name="TPMV" /> which had been brought about by King [[Jafan/Legends|Jafan]] around [[832 BBY/Legends|832 BBY]].<ref name="SWCL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

The Queen would occasionally go twirrling with other [[Lord/Legends|ladies]] of the court on a royal white-furred [[Gualama/Legends|gualama]]. She also possessed a royal herd of guarlaras to ride as well. When she was pictured by T'enna, she rode sidesaddle, with both [[Limb/Legends|legs]] on the same side of the mount, which allowed her to wear fine, flowing clothes fitting to her rank when riding.<ref name="WoSW" />

==Behind the scenes==
The unidentified Queen of Naboo was pictured in ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', a [[2001]] guide written by [[Terryl Whitlatch]] and [[Bob Carrau]], and published by [[Chronicle Books]]. Whitlatch also illustrated the book,<ref name="WoSW" /> reusing many conceptual designs she had originally created for the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TWCC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/bts/profile/f19990210/index.html|text=Terryl Whitlatch: Creature Conjurer}}</ref>

Throughout the Naboo chapter of the guide, the Queen is depicted four times: practicing falconry, mounting a guarlara, riding among a hunting crowd and holding two voorpaks. While the book never explicitly identifies the pictured lady as the Queen, she bears the scar of remembrance,<ref name="WoSW" /> which is a royal attribute.<ref name="TPMV" /> Additionally, the guide does mention that guarlaras are "ridden by monarchy only." Since the foreword of the field journal says that all of T'enna's sketches were done "on-site" and "on the fly," the zoologist must have met the Queen personally.<ref name="WoSW" />
